editorial.headline: The Periodical Publisher’s Clearer Route into Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 58130 covers publishing journals, periodicals and broadcast schedules across formats, with full foreign ownership nationally and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
KBLI 58130 is the publishing home for journals and other periodicals, as well as for the publication of radio and television broadcast schedules. The medium is not the test: the activity may be carried out in print, electronically, digitally, in analogue form or through another publishing format. That makes the code about publishing a recurring editorial or schedule-led product, rather than the technology used to distribute it. Its boundaries are equally useful: independent journalism, independent photojournalism and the production of television or video news programmes sit outside the stated scope.

The registration is open at every scale named in the record—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. In practical terms, the activity can be registered by a business operating at any of those scales, provided its work is genuinely the publishing described here. The scale list signals availability across the spectrum; it does not change the core description of the activity.

At national level, the foreign-investment position is direct. The activity is listed as TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. A foreign investor can therefore hold the activity in full under the national ceiling recorded here. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lesser national cap in this record, so the salient point is not a partial foreign stake but an open activity with a full-ownership ceiling.

In Bali, this is not a case where national openness runs into a provincial PMA-registration ban. The Bali result is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and marked not blocked. The reason is specific: at the Besar scale, OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, placing the activity beyond the provincial moratorium’s target. That moratorium blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI, island-wide and permanently. On the record supplied, 58130 is consequently available for PMA registration in Bali rather than stopped by that rule. The national 100% ceiling remains the national foreign-ownership figure, while Bali’s result here is a risk-based absence of a moratorium block.
editorial.pullQuote: For this activity, national foreign openness is not undone by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
